§C.2 About the Examples

Every rule in the protocol carries worked examples — a page next to the rule it demonstrates, with the Expected Markdown for the region it shows. The expected Markdown is conforming output: it is what a producer should emit, and what ground truth is built from.

Meaning
✅ Sample The rule applies; the Expected Markdown shows what conforming output looks like.
❌ Counter-sample Either it looks like the rule and isn't — the contrast case — or a rendering of it got it wrong (shown as Non-conforming output).

Why counter-samples matter as much as samples

Several rules here exist because two situations look identical on the page and resolve opposite ways. Side-by-side blocks that continue one series are a continuation; side-by-side blocks with their own titles and schemas are separate tables. A wrapped header label looks exactly like a two-row tier. You cannot teach either case with a sample alone — the pair is the lesson.

The most instructive examples are the ones that disagree

Many examples pair a page with an earlier rendering of it. That makes it possible to find pages where the two contradict each other, and those teach a rule far better than a clean case does:

Example What went wrong
3samehead The page prints 32031.9%; the rendering records a plausible-looking 10.9%
3cc The page prints 2.5; the rendering records 25 — a silently dropped decimal
entwick The page prints blank cells; the rendering invents em-dash values for them
3in1 The rendering fabricates a header tier that was never printed
w A rowspan=2 header tier with an empty second row, where one line is printed
wood Visually identical bands tagged as a header in one place and a body cell in another

Each of these is a live illustration of the two failures the whole protocol is built around: never drop, and never invent.

What the examples do not cover

One situation has no worked example, because no example page exercises it yet — Handwriting and Stamps§9.6.5. That note keeps its schematic sketch until a real page turns up.

A few rules have exactly one example rather than several, for the same reason: only one page carries a struck-through value, only one carries a units row, only one shows a header and body disagreeing on column count.

Where the example pages come from

Every image in the protocol is either a synthetic page or a public-domain document.

  • Synthetic pages re-create a situation first found on a real document, with fictional companies, people and figures. Each is an HTML page under tools/synthetic/pages/, rendered by tools/synthetic/render.py; the page is the source, so the Expected Markdown beside the image is correct by construction. Where an example demonstrates an annotation error, the page prints the true value and the extract keeps the documented mistake.
  • Public-domain documents are U.S. federal government works (statistical tables, statutes, court opinions, agency guides, blank federal forms). They are reproduced as published; the credit for each lives in tools/provenance/manifest.json.
  • A few chart families — gantt, sankey, and a clean labeled scatter — carry constructed examples, marked Sample (constructed) and rendered by tools/constructed_charts/.

Each example names its page in backticks, like `3samehead`; that name is the page's stem. tools/provenance/manifest.json records where every image comes from, and the public build (tools/build_site.py --public) refuses to run while any embedded image lacks a cleared entry.

Chart values beyond those printed on the page were measured from the page's vector or pixel geometry (axis calibration by least squares over the axis-label positions, bars from fill rectangles, lines by vertex-snapping at the ticks) — they are not eyeballed.

Adding a new example is covered in SKILL.md — including the rule that you must look at the rendered image before writing a caption about it.

Pages without a paired annotation

Images named bag-<slug>.png show a situation without a full expected annotation beside them; their captions describe only what is printed and never what the annotation should be.
